scenes.spoken_text: Space planning starts with activities and routes. Define functional zones, then compare layouts without concealing openings, services or access requirements.
scenes.caption: Space planning starts with activities and routes. Define functional zones, then compare layouts without concealing openings, services or access requirements.

scenes.spoken_text: List activities, users, timing and required contents. Sketch an initial zone for each without approving unknown furniture dimensions. A functional zone includes the object, its operation and related movement. Check which activities occur together before developing a final arrangement.
scenes.caption: A zone includes the activity, not just the object footprint.

scenes.spoken_text: Identify useful adjacencies, such as storage near work or dining near serving, and separations needed for privacy or quiet. An adjacency diagram expresses priorities, not final distances. Test those relationships in the actual plan with openings, services and circulation before approval.
scenes.caption: Adjacency priorities must be tested in the measured plan.

scenes.display_title: Check the layout through a use sequence
scenes.spoken_text: Trace entry, access to the activity, storage use and exit. Show doors and moving parts in the intended scenarios. Compare alternatives against the same activities and record routes through another activity or inaccessible storage. After relocating a zone, recheck the complete sequence so the clash is not merely displaced.
scenes.caption: Recheck the complete route after moving a zone.

scenes.spoken_text: One room contains a sitting area and work zone. One layout puts the desk on the entry route; another places it near storage clear of the door. Test both against the same user tasks. Decision: prefer the arrangement that supports entry and storage access without interrupting the main activity.
scenes.caption: Decision: prefer the arrangement that supports entry and storage access without interrupting the main activity.
